headline: Your Flexciton waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing semiconductor fabs into the right Flexciton planning-and-scheduling offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Anna Robson, Marketing Director.
productSummary: Flexciton is autonomous production planning and scheduling software for semiconductor manufacturing. Flex Planner uses dynamic capacity modeling and mathematical optimization to turn customer orders and ERP targets into daily wafer start plans, updated every 45 minutes, and to align WIP flow over the next 4 weeks with due dates. Spotlight turns morning meetings into high-impact actions. Flex Local is the local toolset scheduler: set objectives, not parameters, and it balances throughput, cycle time, batching, and reticle moves without rule tuning. Runway turns those schedules into a live load / unload / changeover checklist. Flex Global connects local schedulers, manages timelink constraints, plans changeover campaigns, and shows fab congestion on a heatmap. Homepage customers include Seagate Technology, Renesas, and Microchip. Intel partnership announced on their site. Typical full deployment 6-12 months. 25+ fabs. 40+ experts dedicated to semiconductor manufacturing optimization. 100+ technical publications. 3 patents in mathematical optimization.
coreInsight: Anna already sells autonomous planning and scheduling so chipmakers can stop running the fab on rules, spreadsheets, and firefighting. Mila's original pitch is the TAM: scrape semiconductor manufacturers, write to Operations Managers and Production Directors who need factory-workflow optimization. The one list is semiconductor / wafer-fab employers LinkedIn already lists. The one routing signal is the job-keyword class in their open reqs, because Sales Nav returns that keyword in the same pull and it tells you whether they are staffing production planning / wafer starts, a local toolset scheduler, fab-wide timelink and WIP control, or none of those yet. Ops and production titles are the people layer after the firm is routed. They are not a second TAM.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the keyword already in the job post
sections.takeaway: LinkedIn already names the semiconductor manufacturer and already prints planning, scheduling, photolithography, diffusion, or timelink language in the open req. That keyword is stronger than a headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every semiconductor fab
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Planning / wafer-starts keywords go first, then local scheduling / industrial-engineering keywords, then timelink / WIP / fab-wide keywords, then every remaining in-TAM semiconductor manufacturer.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each job keyword gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Planning hiring gets a wafer-starts plan brief. Toolset-scheduling hiring gets a Flex Local KPI map. Timelink / WIP hiring gets a Flex Global cascade. The rest get the autonomous-factory playbook Mila already pitched to ops and production directors.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Kill the spreadsheet plan, stop retuning rules, connect the toolsets
sections.takeaway: The list is always semiconductor manufacturers, aimed at operations managers, production directors, industrial engineers, and fab / manufacturing leads. Fab type is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes: throughput language versus on-time-delivery language, which is the test Mila already named.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the req they already posted
sections.takeaway: Notice the keyword, poke the spreadsheet / rules / timelink gap that keyword implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the planning keyword first
sections.takeaway: Start where they are already staffing the plan-versus-floor gap Flex Planner is built for. Prove reply density, then roll toolset scheduling, timelink / WIP, and the autonomous-factory catch-all.

signalReasons: LinkedIn Sales Nav job search is the TAM Mila already named, semiconductor manufacturers with a visible ops or production lead, and the planning-or-scheduling keyword in one pull.

The same pull returns production planning / wafer starts / APS / capacity, industrial engineering / dispatch / toolset scheduling / photolithography, or timelink / QTimer / WIP / factory automation, which is enough to route without a second enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Flexciton copy: Flex Planner (ERP targets to daily wafer starts every 45 minutes), Flex Local (objectives not parameters, Runway on the shop floor), Flex Global (timelinks, heatmap, changeover campaigns), and the homepage autonomy pitch for everyone else.
Ops title, industrial-engineer title, and fab type are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last, never the TAM spine.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Planning / wafer-starts keyword
tiers.trigger: LinkedIn job post names production planning, wafer starts, capacity planning, APS, advanced planning, on-time delivery, WIP planning, or production control. Keyword class estimated, not a Flexciton site field.
tiers.pain: They are staffing the plan. Starts still take days in spreadsheets, and static capacity models do not survive the next tool-down. Flex Planner page: replace days of manual planning with constraint-aware wafer start plans delivered autonomously and updated every 45 minutes. No spreadsheets, no firefighting, no delay. Their comparison table: legacy starts planning takes days and multiple people with continuous firefighting.
tiers.valueProp: Flex Planner aligns WIP flow over the next 4 weeks with real capacity and customer due dates. Planner page: 10% reduction in cycle time at any given WIP level, 30% reduction in standard deviation from target velocity. Spotlight gives planners high-impact recommendations, from rescheduling maintenance to qualifying recipes. Mark Patton, Director of Manufacturing, Seagate Technology, on the homepage: with Flexciton they improved predictability of delivery by meeting weekly customer commits.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They already budgeted a role to keep the plan honest against the floor.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Toolset-scheduling keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names industrial engineer, dispatch, toolset scheduler, photolithography, photo area, reticle, batching, recipe enablement, or shop-floor scheduling, and no planning_capacity keyword. Class estimated.
tiers.pain: They already schedule the toolset. Rules and parameter tweaks eat industrial-engineering time every time the fab state changes. Flex Local page: say goodbye to manual rules and constant parameter tweaking. Their comparison table: legacy solutions take 50%-80% of 1 Eng FTE to understand and re-tune at every change in fab state, and 2-3 years to full deployment versus typically 12 months for Flex Local.
tiers.valueProp: Flex Local lets the fab set objectives, not parameters, and autonomously balances throughput, cycle time, batching, and reticle moves. Runway turns the schedule into a live load / unload / changeover checklist. Homepage and Local page: 9.4% increase in throughput in the photo area. Jay Maguire, Industrial Engineer, Renesas Electronics, on the homepage: pleased with the decision to partner with Flexciton to improve scheduling decision making, implementation better than hoped.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. They already pay industrial engineers to keep rules alive. Flex Local is built to retire that loop.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Timelink / WIP keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names timelink, QTimer, queue timer, diffusion, furnace batch, factory automation, MES dispatch integration, or fab-wide WIP, and no planning_capacity or toolset_scheduling keyword. Class estimated.
tiers.pain: Local dispatch cannot see the next toolset. Timelinks get violated, batches stay small, WIP piles up in the wrong place. Flex Global page: timelink constraints are too complex for rule-based schedulers. Frontend page: wafers can only spend a certain amount of time between two or more process steps, and engineers must balance throughput, queue time, and batch sizes pulling in opposite directions.
tiers.valueProp: Flex Global connects local schedulers, gets the right WIP to the right tool at the right time, and shows congestion on a heatmap. Homepage and Global page: 29% reduction in timelink violations in the diffusion area, 18% increase in batch size across the diffusion area. Global page quote: improve predictability and linearity, key to meeting commits consistently.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. They are already staffing the fab-wide constraint Flex Global is built for.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining TAM
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM semiconductor manufacturer: visible operations manager, production director, director of manufacturing, or fab manager, and none of the keywords above.
tiers.pain: They are still in the chipmaker set Mila named. Factory workflow still means rules, firefighting, and a plan that dies on contact with the floor. Homepage: using rules-based legacy software or manual methods can lead to reduced efficiency and damaged KPIs. Frontend page: an APS system must evaluate billions of possible scenarios and identify the best solution every few minutes.
tiers.valueProp: Flexciton replaces reactive systems with autonomous plans and schedules. Homepage: 25+ fabs, 40+ experts dedicated to semiconductor manufacturing optimization, 100+ technical publications, 3 patents. Typical full deployment 6-12 months, with value early in the process. Named customers on the homepage: Seagate Technology, Renesas, and Microchip. Intel partnership is on their resources list.
tiers.dataSource: LinkedIn TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

launchPlan: Pull LinkedIn Sales Nav for semiconductor manufacturers and wafer fabs with a visible Operations Manager, Production Director, Director of Manufacturing, Industrial Engineer, Production Controller, Capacity Planner, or Fab Manager, or with planning / scheduling / APS jobs. Keep the open-req keyword in the same export. Classify job_keyword_class as planning_capacity, toolset_scheduling, timelink_wip, or none. Suppress already_customer when a Flexciton deployment is visible. Named case-study logos (Seagate, Renesas, Microchip) are not a blanket exclude.

Keyword classes are estimated GTMx taxonomy, not Flexciton site fields. Tune the synonym list after the first Sales Nav pull if a band is starved or overlapping. First match wins. Do not also route on headcount, wafer starts, or fab revenue. Those cutoffs are not on flexciton.com.

Resolve work emails in Apollo only after the domain is routed. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM. Optional careers-page text fills {{fab_type}} (frontend, backend, IDM, foundry, photo, diffusion) as a merge tag only.

Launch Tier 1 Wafer Starts Plan Brief first. Smallest list, sharpest plan-versus-floor signal, closest to Flex Planner (ERP to daily starts every 45 minutes). Spreadsheet copy as the control, Seagate on-time-commit copy as the A/B on the same list.
Add Tier 2 Toolset KPI Map once {{named_keyword}} merge tags are clean across industrial-engineer, dispatch, photo, and batching language. Then Tier 3 Timelink Cascade Brief.

Turn on the Autonomous Factory Playbook catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM semiconductor manufacturer still has a route. That is Mila's original ops / production-director factory-workflow pitch. Keep fab_type as a merge tag, not a campaign split, until one job-keyword tier is clearly working. Do not launch a tier under about 1,500 contacts. That threshold is the waterfall SOP, not a Flexciton site number.
